properties.name: Tower Rush
properties.description: Blast a path through stone with your tracked tower before the gas cloud catches you.

content.text:
Hold and drag to aim and fire
Mouse: aim, hold left button

events.comment: TOWER RUSH - Phase 1 prototype. Every system is an external event (Project manager > External events), included here in this order. Tuning numbers are the global variable Tuning; formations are the global variable Formations.

RUN MANAGER - owns: State ("Run" / "Over"), Dt, StartX, Distance, BestDistance, NewBest, OverTime.
Starts the run, ends it (GameOver is requested by CloudController through State), saves the best distance (storage "TowerRush") and restarts the scene.
Dt is the frame time, capped so a slow frame can never make the tower or a bullet skip through a cell. Every system moves things with Dt, never with a fixed step per frame.
Restart reloads the scene, which resets every run variable and object. The short delay stops the finger that was firing when the cloud hit from pressing Restart by accident.

OBSTACLE GENERATOR - owns: NextFormationX, FormationCount, FormationIndex, Shape, ShapeW, ShapeRows, SpawnX, Idx, Col, Row, Ch, CellsSpawned.
Formations are text grids in the global variable Formations (one string per formation, rows separated by |, top row first, the bottom row sits on the ground). Each character is a cell: a material's Char (# Stone, H Hardstone, C Concrete, M Metal, G Glass, W Wood), . empty. A lower-case letter is a partly drawn square of that material: Tuning.PartialHP (1) shot whatever the material.
Cell is a 12 x 12 tiled sprite. Text-grid formations show their material's tile; art formations (Texture set, made by tools/import_formations.py from whole pixel-art pictures) show their own 12 x 12 slice of the picture: the cell's X/Y offset is its column/row times 12.

events.name: Spawn the next formation ahead of the camera

events.comment: FormationDeck lists every formation as many times as its Weight (art/formations/<name>.json {"weight": 2}). The first Tuning.EasyStart formations of a run come from EasyDeck (lane cost up to Tuning.EasyLaneShots shots). The same formation never comes twice in a row.
Preview one formation (e.g. your new art): set Tuning.TestFormation to its index in Formations. -1 = normal game.

events.name: Art formations: give the new cells their picture
Embed gems in some of the new cells

events.comment: GEMS (Phase 2): with chance Tuning.GemChance a new formation hides GemsMin..GemsMax gems. A gem goes in a cell above the tower's lane with chance GemAboveLaneChance (more time to dig it out), else anywhere in the formation. The type is drawn by the Weight of each entry in the global Gems.
Sometimes the next formation follows right behind (a cluster).
Everything behind the left edge of the screen is gone for good (the cloud is there).

TOWER CONTROLLER - owns: TowerStep, Blocked.
The tower drives right at Tuning.TowerSpeed. Each frame it moves, and if its collision mask (the chassis, 44 x 80 px) now overlaps any surviving Cell it moves back and counts as blocked. A step is at most TowerSpeed x MaxFrameTime (about 4 px), smaller than a cell, so it can never skip through one. The tower fits through an opening at least 7 cells (84 px) high.

TURRET CONTROLLER - owns: PivotX/Y, AimX/Y, TargetAngle, TurretAngle, InputTouch, LastTouchTime, HasAimed, Firing, FireCooldown, AimOffset, ShotsFired.
Mouse: the cursor is the aim point, hold the left button to fire.
Touch: press anywhere below the top bar and drag; the aim point is AimOffset px above the finger so the target stays visible (change it with the AIM button, saved in storage).
The turret pivots on the Tower sprite's point TurretMount (move it in the sprite editor to match the art). The turret and bullets never collide with the tower: bullets only ray-cast against Cells and are drawn above the tower. The angle is kept between straight left (-180), up, and TurretMaxDown (88 = almost straight down, in front), turning through the top only.
A real touch switches to touch aiming. A mouse press switches back, unless a finger was down in the last second (phones also send an imitation mouse click after a tap).
CursorX/CursorY of the base layer are world coordinates: they already include the camera scroll, so the aim stays exact while the world moves.
Down-and-back angles (aiming under or behind the tower) snap to the nearest allowed one.

PROJECTILE SYSTEM - owns: BulletStep, BulletHit, HitX, HitY.
Bullets are moved by a ray, not by forces: each frame a ray is cast from the bullet along its path for the distance it travels this frame (BulletSpeed x Dt). The first Cell the ray meets is hit - only that one - so a fast bullet can never pass through a thin cell. A new bullet starts at the turret pivot and its first ray also covers the barrel (Extra), so it leaves at the muzzle and still hits a cell touching the barrel.
A gem is released only when the cell holding it breaks; GemSystem takes it from here.
Damage shows as a crack overlay (one shared image for every material and picture), linked to its cell so it goes when the cell goes.

events.name: Bullets that leave the play area

events.comment:
OBSTACLE GRID - owns: CellsDestroyed, CellsSpawned, the Cell object variables (HP, MaxHP, Material, Flash) and the hit effects.
Every Cell is its own 12 x 12 object with its own collision box, so a destroyed cell stops blocking at once and the tower can drive through any tunnel big enough for its chassis. Damage is shown by a Crack overlay (animations Crack1, Crack2) linked to the cell.

GEM SYSTEM - owns: RunGems, TotalGems, GemsCollected, GemsLost, GemsSaved, GemDX/DY/Dist/Step and the Gem / GemPopup objects once a gem is released (ProjectileSystem creates it when its cell breaks).
A released gem pops out, falls and bounces on the ground. Once within Tuning.PickupRadius of the tower's centre it flies to the tower and its value is added to the run (no tapping). Gems left behind the screen are lost. At game over the run's gems are added to TotalGems (storage).

events.name: Bank the run's gems at game over

events.comment:
CLOUD CONTROLLER - owns: CloudX, CloudGap.
The cloud is a wall of gas at world position CloudX (its right edge). It moves right at Tuning.CloudSpeed all the time, whatever the tower does; it starts Tuning.CloudStartGap px behind the back of the chassis. When it reaches the chassis the run ends.
After the run ends the cloud rolls on a little to swallow the tower.

CAMERA AND HUD - reads the other systems' variables, owns nothing else.
The camera follows the tower horizontally with the tower in the left part of the screen (Tuning.CameraLead), so the next formations are visible. The ground and far hills are tiled sprites that follow the camera.

actions.comment: Ground and far layer cover the screen and slide their picture: the ground moves with the world, the far layer at 30 % (parallax). Any image width tiles seamlessly.

events.comment: Tuning.ShowFarLayer = 0 hides the scrolling far skyline (when the sky picture has its own).
